explanation: Starting at one cell, only matching neighbors can extend its original-color component. Mark a matching cell by recoloring it before adding it to a work stack. This makes every cell enter the work stack once and avoids a separate visited matrix. The same-color early return is necessary because recoloring would otherwise fail to mark visits.
correctness: After the initial bounds and same-color checks, the start cell belongs to the required component and is marked. Every later pushed cell is an original-color neighbor of an already reached cell, so it belongs to that component. Recoloring at discovery prevents a second push. Conversely, take any cell in the component and a connecting path from the start: induction along that path ensures each next original-color neighbor is eventually discovered. Thus every and only component cells are recolored. No row or outer array is replaced, and all other cell values are untouched.
walkthrough: With [[1,0,1],[0,1,1],[1,1,0]], start (0,0) and newColor 2. Its right and lower neighbors are both 0, so only that one cell changes, giving [[2,0,1],[0,1,1],[1,1,0]]. The 1 at (1,1) touches diagonally but is outside the region.
timeComplexity: O(k) fill time for a changed component of k cells, with four neighbor checks per cell; O(1) fill work for invalid coordinates or equal colors. The C++ by-value result adds O(rows*columns) return-copy time even for a no-op.
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary work-stack storage, at most O(rows*columns). The C++ by-value return additionally copies the O(rows*columns) screen values; other languages return the existing screen object.
edgeCases: Diagonal-only contact must not spread paint.
Same-color request, empty screen, zero-width rows, and out-of-bounds signed coordinates.
Whole-screen component, isolated cell, and adjacent different-color regions.
